title: Enterprise FAPI OAuth 2.0 & OIDC Authorization Server with DPoP (RFC 9449), PAR (RFC 9126), and PKCE
objective: Implement an enterprise-scale, Financial-grade API (FAPI) compliant OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect Authorization Framework in Python/FastAPI using SQLite and Cryptography. The framework must be partitioned into a multi-module architecture across core crypto, DPoP validation, PAR orchestration, token family lineage tracking, and REST endpoints. The engine must support RFC 7636 S256 PKCE, RFC 6749 grant workflows, Strict Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) with cascading family invalidation, RFC 9449 DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession at the Application Layer) token binding and replay prevention, RFC 9126 PAR (Pushed Authorization Requests), RFC 7517/8414 JWKS key rotation, RFC 7662 Introspection, and RFC 7009 Revocation.
motivation: Financial-grade API (FAPI) security profiles (Open Banking, Healthcare, Zero-Trust identity) mandate cryptographic proof-of-possession (DPoP), pushed authorization (PAR), and strict token rotation to eliminate bearer token theft and man-in-the-middle exploits. Implementing this end-to-end tests advanced asymmetric cryptography, protocol state machines, distributed replay protection, and multi-package software architecture.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Multi-Module FAPI Architecture: Coordinating modular subsystems across core crypto (RSA/ECDSA key pairs, JWK thumbprints), DPoP proof verification (jti replay caches, HTTP URI/method binding, ath hash calculation), PAR lifecycle (60s request_uri caching), and token family lineage storage.
2. RFC 9449 DPoP Cryptographic Proof-of-Possession: Parsing client-generated ephemeral DPoP JWT proofs, verifying public JWK headers, computing SHA-256 access token hashes (ath), enforcing timestamp freshness, and binding the client's JWK thumbprint (jkt) to minted RS256 JWT access tokens.
3. Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR, RFC 9126) & Cascade Invalidation: Securely exchanging authorization request payloads for short-lived, single-use request_uris while maintaining atomic SQLite transactions and instant cascading family revocation upon refresh token reuse.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11-slim container with FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pytest, Cryptography, PyJWT, HTTPX, SQLite3, and multi-module package scaffolding across /app/core, /app/services, /app/api, and /app/models.
oracleStrategy: Reference multi-package implementation under solution/ featuring modular DPoP verifiers, PAR request managers, RSA key rotation pipelines, SQLite token lineage databases, and RFC-compliant REST controllers.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh executing 7 comprehensive hidden pytest test suites testing:
1. RFC 9126 Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR) and single-use request_uri exchange.
2. RFC 7636 S256 PKCE authorization code grant with unpadded Base64URL validation.
3. Strict Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) and cascading token family replay attack invalidation.
4. RFC 9449 DPoP Proof-of-Possession validation, ath thumbprint binding, and jti replay rejection.
5. OIDC Discovery & multi-key JWKS rotation.
6. RFC 7662 Token Introspection and RFC 7009 Token Revocation.
7. Client Credentials and RFC 8628 Device Authorization Flow.
binarySuccessCondition: Passes 100% of all hidden test suites across all 7 FAPI specification domains with full reward score >= 0.95.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 15%: RFC 9126 Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR).
- 15%: PKCE Authorization Code Grant & Base64URL strictness.
- 15%: Strict Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) & family reuse detection.
- 20%: RFC 9449 DPoP Proof-of-Possession & jti replay prevention.
- 15%: JWKS Discovery & multi-key RSA token verification.
- 10%: RFC 7662 Introspection & RFC 7009 Revocation.
- 10%: Device Authorization Flow & Client Credentials.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Unbound DPoP tokens: Verifier presents valid access tokens with mismatched or expired DPoP proofs to ensure 401 rejection.
2. PAR payload mutation: Verifier alters authorization parameters post-PAR issuance to ensure strict parameter binding.
